2012_036_051512spmtg.paragraph: Agenda and full board packet for the Troy School District Special Board of Education meeting held Tuesday, May 15, 2012 at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. The bulk of the packet is a five-part technology bid award package funding a 'Troy Cloud' virtual desktop expansion out of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, plus a report on and resolution supporting the proposed Oakland Intermediate School District budget and a Public Act 419 election resolution. The technology purchases listed in the supporting memo carry a stated total cost of $1,766,591.92, with the largest single award being $750,876.40 to Netech for storage expansion.

**Meeting**
Special Board of Education meeting, Tuesday, May 15, 2012, 6:00 P.M., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public communication is limited to one-half hour each for agenda and non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Recognition**
Sara Ma, a junior at Troy High School, received a bronze medal as a Distinguished Finalist in the Prudential Spirit of Community Awards for her work promoting tolerance and diversity. Hitesh Parikh, representing Prudential Financial, presented the award.

**Technology bids (opened April 26, 2012; 2004 Capital Projects / Bond Fund)**
Bid openings were overseen by Ken Miller (Executive Director of Facilities), Sara Konieczka (Purchasing Supervisor) and Merri Lynn Colligan (Director of Technology); purchasing memos dated May 9, 2012 went to Assistant Superintendent Mark S. Rajter.

| Bid | Item | Award | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9729 | Server expansion (UCS, 1250 more VDI users) | Data Strategy | $161,305.35 |
| 9729 MA#1 | VMware licensing (Statewide Cooperative Bid) | Merit | $172,230.24 |
| 9730 | 675 Zero Clients | Data Strategy | $203,539.50 |
| 9731 | EMC VMAXe storage expansion | Netech | $750,876.40 |
| 9732 | Teacher desktop computers | Netech | $473,515.00 |

Competing server bids were Information Systems Intelligence at $121,463.58 and Netech at $146,828.37. Zero Client alternatives were UltraLevel $230,850.00, Inacomp $128,250.00 and Netech $261,225.00; testing found the HP Smart Client offered by Inacomp did not match the Wyse P20 with Qomo, Elmo and digital-camera peripherals. Storage bids scaled for 1,500 VDI users with Avamar backup were Data Strategy $754,183.03, Netech $750,876.40 and CDW $756,927.67. Teacher desktop bids included CDW $668,137.00, Intel Corp (Aces Computers) $518,397.05, Inacomp $470,255.00 and Netech $473,515.00; CDI submitted no base bid.

**Desktop replacement plan**
A May 8, 2012 memo recommends 1057 Troy Cloud virtualized desktops for general use labs, 135 office workstations with Zero Clients, and 795 new teacher workstation computers, with Zero Clients in 3 labs each at Athens and Troy High Schools, 2 labs at each middle school, 1 lab at IAE and 2 labs at Niles. VMware maintenance runs $22 per client per year. Additional anticipated costs: Trend antivirus $15,000.00, Microsoft VDA operating system licensing $19,000.00, security cables and mounting hardware $50,000.00, and a pending electrical estimate for the Services Building head end (IDS engaged).

**Oakland Schools FY 2012-13 proposed budget (Section 624 report)**
Total revenue $270.7 million; total expenditures $272.79 million. General Education Fund revenue $17.4 million against $17.8 million of expenditures; Special Education Fund $128.2 million both ways; Career Focused Education Fund revenue $31.6 million against $32.2 million. Property tax collections declined 23.9% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, an accumulated loss of $191.6 million against a FY 2008 base levy of $216.9 million. Total Oakland Schools bonded debt is $60,317,500.

**Other actions**
The Board adopted a resolution expressing support for the Oakland ISD budget solely to comply with Section 624, to be forwarded by June 1, 2012, and a Public Act 419 resolution designating Todd Miletti as its representative to the 2012 Oakland Schools electoral body, supporting Mark Katz, Dr. Theresa Rich and George Ehlert; that vote carried 6-0 with Underwood absent.

Agenda and complete supporting packet for the Troy School District Special Board of Education meeting of Tuesday, May 15, 2012, convened at 6:00 P.M. at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). The agenda ran: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (Prudential Spirit of the Community Award); Additions and Deletions; Public Communication on agenda items; General Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business items A through G; Public Communication on non-agenda items; Other; and Adjournment. Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and may be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, with each speaker allowed up to three minutes.

RECOGNITION. The Prudential Spirit of Community Awards program is described as the largest youth recognition program in the United States based exclusively on volunteer community service, honoring middle level and high school students at local, state and national levels. Sara Ma, a junior at Troy High School, was awarded a bronze medal and recognized as a Distinguished Finalist for her work promoting tolerance and diversity. Hitesh Parikh, representing Prudential Financial, presented the medal.

TECHNOLOGY BID PACKAGE. Five business items awarded bids opened April 26, 2012, all designated as 2004 Capital Projects Fund / 2004 Bond Fund expenditures. Every bid opening was overseen by Ken Miller, Executive Director of Facilities; Sara Konieczka, Purchasing Supervisor; and Merri Lynn Colligan, Director of Technology (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, 248/823-5090). Purchasing memoranda dated May 9, 2012 from Sara L. Konieczka (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077) were directed to Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent; technology memoranda were addressed to Superintendent Dr. Barbara Fowler.

Item 8.A, Bid #9729 Server Expansion. Bids were sent to eighteen potential bidders for expansion of the existing UCS infrastructure to support 1250 additional virtual desktop users; three vendors responded, none of them a no bid, and the award is based on total cumulative price. Base bids: Data Strategy $161,305.35; Information Systems Intelligence $121,463.58; Netech $146,828.37. For furnishing and installing 10 B200 M3 servers the quoted amounts were Data Strategy $166,430.78, Information Systems Intelligence $150,714.74 and Netech $145,544.83. Data Strategy was recommended because its base bid proposed 10 servers with a higher processor and a design consistent with the manufacturer's recommendation for 1250 virtual desktops, it holds technical certifications for Cisco, VMware and EMC, its references were validated, it maintains a local office for warranty support, and it offers a free annual health check during the warranty period. The suggested resolution awards the server expansion bid to Data Strategy in the amount of $161,305.35.

Item 8.B, VMware Licensing (Bid #9729 Mandatory Alternate #1). Bids for the mandatory alternate were Data Strategy $305,042.14, Netech $324,625.00 and Information Systems Intelligence $353,391.45, against a Statewide Cooperative Bid price from Merit of $172,230.24. The resolution awards VMware licensing to Merit in the amount of $172,230.24.

Item 8.C, Bid #9730 Zero Client. Four vendors responded for Zero Clients supporting virtual desktop users in offices and secondary general purpose labs. For furnishing and installing 675 Zero Clients: UltraLevel $230,850.00 (no base bid), Data Strategy $203,539.50 (base bid $385,500.00, unit price $301.54), Inacomp $128,250.00 (base bid $247,000.00, unit price $190.00) and Netech $261,225.00 (base bid $477,100.00, unit price $387.00). Post-bid interviews and demo unit testing found the HP Smart Client recommended in the Inacomp bid did not perform to the same standard as the Wyse P20 client when connected to Qomo and Elmo devices and digital cameras, and HP technical support left the issues unresolved. The resolution awards the zero client bid to Data Strategy in the amount of $203,539.50.

Item 8.D, Bid #9731 Storage Expansion. Three vendors bid on expansion of the existing EMC VMAXe infrastructure. Base bids for 2000 users were Data Strategy $799,500.00, Netech $799,800.00 and CDW $792,269.00; base bids scaled for 1,500 VDI users were $673,583.03, $665,800.00 and $676,622.67 respectively; Mandatory Alternate 4 (Avamar backup expansion) came in at $80,600.00, $85,076.40 and $80,305.00; and combined storage for 1500 plus Avamar backup totaled $754,183.03 (Data Strategy), $750,876.40 (Netech) and $756,927.67 (CDW). The district stated it has enough storage for existing clients up to 750 users, requested a base bid covering 1250 additional users, received bids priced for 2000 additional users, and after post-bid interviews and design verification with the manufacturer used unit pricing to size for an additional 1500 VDI users. The resolution awards storage expansion to Netech in the amount of $750,876.40. Line-item quote comparisons cover EMC VMAXe components including the VMAXe ENGINE 96GB UPG ($44,200.00 CDW, $46,514.22 DSI, $48,000.00 Netech) and PREMIUM SOFTWARE SUPPORT PLATFORM/ELM ($139,543.00, $78,580.01, $77,500.00).

Item 8.E, Bid #9732 Teacher Desktop Computers. Seven vendors responded and two did not meet bid specification. Summary figures: CDW $668,137.00; Intel Corp (Aces Computers) $518,397.05; Netech base bid $502,885.00 with a video card deduction of ($44.00) each, video cable at $8.00 each, a video change cost of ($29,340.00) and a total award of $473,515.00; CDI no base bid; Inacomp base bid $487,370.00 with ($39.00) each deduct, $18.00 each cable, ($17,115.00) video change cost and $470,255.00 total. On-board graphics were judged sufficient to support Qomo and Smart Board connections. Netech was recommended for the base bid and video card deduction so the district can self-maintain the desktops using its Dell certified technicians; the resolution awards $473,515.00.

DESKTOP REPLACEMENT MEMO (May 8, 2012, Merri Lynn Colligan). Cited benefits of cloud-based virtual desktops include remote access from any device, easier software deployment, flexible allocation of specifications, reduced electrical cost through lower Zero Client power consumption, and swap-out end-device support. Ongoing virtualized costs include VMware license maintenance at $22 per client per year plus storage and server infrastructure maintenance; ROI studies are cited for districts elongating hardware life by two to three years and experiencing a 40-50% decrease in ongoing maintenance cost. Districts named as deploying virtualized desktops: Chippewa Valley, Clawson, Rockford, and Central Michigan University. Replacement recommendations: General Use Lab, 1057 Troy Cloud Virtualized Desktops, with Zero Clients in 3 labs at Athens and Troy High Schools, 2 labs at each middle school, 1 lab at IAE and 2 labs at Niles, and reimaging of existing hardware in remaining secondary labs; Office Workstation 135 Troy Cloud Virtualized Desktops with Zero Client; Teacher Workstation 795 new computers, noting teacher workstations connected to Smart Boards are not currently candidates for virtualization. The purchase list shows server expansion $166,430.78, teacher desktops $473,515.00, storage expansion $750,876.40, Zero Clients $203,539.50 and VMware view licensing for 1250 users $172,230.24, with a stated Total Cost of $1,766,591.92. Additional anticipated costs are Trend antivirus for VMware desktops $15,000.00, Microsoft VDA operating system licensing $19,000.00, security cables and mounting hardware $50,000.00, and a pending estimate for electrical adjustments at the District head end in the Services Building, for which IDS has been engaged.

SUPERINTENDENT GOAL #3 (2011-2012), DATA PROCESSING COST ANALYSIS. A memo from Mark S. Rajter, Business Services (4400 Livernois, 248/823-4010, fax 248/823-4013) to Barbara Fowler, Ph.D., Superintendent, describes a department of three staff, two technical programmers (one serving as department manager) and one support person, supporting eSchoolPlus (student information), FinancePlus (financial/human resources), third-party applications, databases, operating systems, data requests, state and federal reporting, internally developed web applications and general district support. Three analytic prongs are described: continued self-operation, third-party hosting from the vendor or another user, and a possible Oakland Schools RFP for Finance/HR software. Troy will pursue collaboration with one of the other 5 districts/ISDs in Michigan using SunGard FinancePlus, expected to be completed by fall 2012. The attached model shows an eSchool finance payment financed over 5 years 2010-2015 at $41,381, $38,760, $36,140 and $33,518; standard software maintenance/support of $50,345, $110,700 and $86,100; SunGard software maintenance/support $11,925; hardware maintenance $3,500; and TSD labor lines JS $111,625/$19,357, IB $76,099/$14,541 and JM $62,882/$14,189, with Total Student Info System figures of $312,876 and $316,376 and a $62,270 column. Finance-system lines include standard software maintenance/support $21,923, $45,225 and $57,285, custom software maintenance/support $11,282, SunGard maintenance $11,416/$11,415, IBM Informix database $2,900, HP 9000 server hardware maintenance $6,791, and labor of JS $17,421, IB $20,843, JM $1,612, with Total Finance System entries of $94,188, $45,225, $147,600 and $183,746. Combined Total Student and Finance rows show $407,064, $204,545, $155,925, $144,720, $177,956; $410,563, $131,325, $183,746; $143,385; and $156,458. Alternative pricing footnotes: Zangle at $9 per student the first year and $7 per student thereafter with no report writer and no SQL access, first-line support through Oakland and second-line through Wayne RESA; AMS at $3.75 per student for the first 3 years then $4.75 per student; Lenawee at $12 per student for eSchoolPlus and FinancePlus using 12,300 FTE; and SunGard SaaS covering both products with a SIF agent, no SQL access, and a FinPlus 5.0 upgrade needed at additional cost. Per-student comparisons list student cost of $25.44, $8.97, $9.00, $25.72, $7.00 and $5.06; Fin/HR cost of $7.66, $3.68, $12.00, $14.47, $14.94 and $4.66; and combined student, finance and HR costs of $33.09, $16.63, $12.68, $12.00, $14.47, $33.38, $10.68, $14.94, $11.66 and $12.72.

ITEM 8.F, OAKLAND SCHOOLS PROPOSED FY 2012-2013 BUDGET REPORT (presented by Mark Rajter, no action required). Under Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624), effective 2004, each ISD must submit its proposed budget to constituent district boards by May 1 and each constituent board must adopt a resolution of support or disapproval by June 1 and mail it to the Oakland Schools Board of Education. The property tax forecast from base year FY 2008 shows FY 2008-09 -.0075% and $-, FY 2009-10 -3.8% and $(8.2)M, FY 2010-11 -11.9% and $(32.9)M, FY 2011-12 -7.5% and $(46.7)M, FY 2012-13 -3.0% and $(51.8)M, FY 2013-14 0%, FY 2014-15 0%, FY 2015-16 2% and FY 2016-17 1%. Annual property tax collection declined from FY 2008 to FY 2014 by 23.9%, an accumulative loss of $191.6 million; the FY 2008 base year tax levy was $216.9 million and the FY 2014 expected tax levy is $165.08 million. Revenue assumptions include a 3% property tax revenue decrease, expected interest earnings of $895K for all funds combined (compared with $7.7 million in FY 2007), increased local district utilization of the student application and NextGen Exchange student programs, stable revenue from GenNet, Rubicon West and Discovery/Learn 360 online software, stable General Education Section 81 revenue, stable Special Education and Career Focused Education state funding, and no personal property tax loss forecast in FY13. Total FY 2013 revenue is $270.7 Million and total expenditures $272.79 Million across P.S./Supplies, Grants, Personnel and Transfers to LEAs. General Education Fund revenue totals $17.4 Million (property tax $9.8M or 56% of total revenue, other local $3.5M, state sources $3.5M, other financing sources $.6M) against expenditures of $17.8 Million (General Administration $1.5M, Finance and Operations $6.8M, Instructional Services $8.8M, plant and fixed charges and transfers to LEAs $.7M). The Special Education Fund shows revenue of $128.2 Million (property tax $124.7M or 97%, other local $.8M, state $2.5M, other financing $.2M) and expenditures of $128.2 Million (program supervision and direction $2.3M, program operations $7.1M, plant and fixed charges $8M, LEA transfers and program subsidies $110.8M). FY 2013 special education program support and subsidies are PA-18 Base Distribution $108,560,000, Extraordinary Contingency $100,000, Section 24 subsidy/other $100,000, Group Homes $1,200,000, Havenwick $150,000 and SEI Regional Day Treatment $450,000, totaling $110,560,600; the PA-18 Base Distribution declined $(4.1M) from FY 2012. FY 2013 district debt lists GEF debt principal of $4,030,000 with an average annual payment of $765,000, CFEF debt principal of $42,875,000 with $3,100,000, QSCB debt principal of $13,412,500 with $1,111,000, and total Oakland Schools bonded debt of $60,317,500 with $4,976,000; debt service for the 2003 Administration Building Project Bond and the QSCB issue is pre-funded in Debt Service Funds 310 and 313, and debt service for the 2007 campus renovations bond is pre-funded in Debt Service Fund 312 through FY 2020.

ITEM 8.G, APPROVAL OF THE OAKLAND ISD BUDGET. The resolution recites the Section 624 review requirement and states that the Troy Board of Education has received and reviewed the proposed ISD budget and expresses its support, while stating its belief that the Intermediate School District is responsible for its own operations including adoption of its budget and that Troy's support is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624. The secretary is directed to forward the resolution to the intermediate school board or its superintendent no later than June 1, 2012, and conflicting resolutions are rescinded.

OAKLAND SCHOOLS BIENNIAL ELECTION RESOLUTION. The packet reproduces the prior June 1, 2010 resolution, moved by Nancy Philippart and supported by Paula Fleming, which designated Mr. Todd Miletti as representative to the 2010 electoral body and supported Mrs. Barbara DeMarco and Mr. Connie R. Williams, CPA, FHFMA, for six-year terms ending June 30, 2016 and Dr. Theresa Rich for a partial term of two years ending June 30, 2012, adopted with 7 ayes and 0 nays for the June 7, 2010 election. The 2012 resolution, considered at the open meeting of Tuesday, May 15, 2012 under Public Act 419 of 2004, designates Mr. Todd Miletti as Troy's representative to the 2012 electoral body, supports Mr. Mark Katz and Dr. Theresa Rich for six-year terms ending June 30, 2018 and Mr. George Ehlert for a partial term of two years ending June 30, 2014, and directs Miletti to vote for those three at least on the first ballot at the June 4 election. The roll call recorded Hauff yes, Miletti yes, Philippart yes, Underwood absent, Edmunds yes, Fleming yes and Schmidt yes; the motion carried 6-0. A blank sample resolution, to be adopted on or after May 14th, is attached.

CANDIDATE BIOGRAPHIES. Theresa Rich, Ph.D., of Farmington Hills, has been employed at General Motors for 28 years including a decade practicing law and nearly two decades in Human Resources, currently as Organization Development Manager and executive coach leading a global team across more than 60 countries; she was appointed and then elected an Oakland Schools trustee in 2010 and serves on the Farmington/Farmington Hills Foundation for Youth and Families (trustee since 2001, allocations chair since 2006) and the Oakland Schools Education Foundation (since 2010). She authored Staying Sane in Crazy Times and a chapter in the Handbook of Research on Electronic Collaboration and Organizational Synergy, has been adjunct faculty at Michigan State University and Wayne State University, and holds a PhD in Organization and Management from Capella University, an LL.M. in Taxation and a Juris Doctor from Wayne State University, an MBA and BBA from Grand Valley State University, and an Associate of Business Administration in Accounting from Lake Michigan College, which named her its 2006 Clarence Beckwith Distinguished Alumni of the Year. Her husband is Brian Rich; son Zachary is entering the Wayne State University Irvin D. Reid Honors College and daughter Alyson is in the International Academy class of 2014. Marc D. Katz of 2350 Oxford Road, Berkley, MI 48072-1740 (248.219.5949, marcgoblue1@gmail.com) is a candidate for the six-year term beginning July 1, 2012 and expiring June 30, 2018; he served on the Berkley Board of Education from July 1, 1990 to December 31, 2011 as President, Vice President, Treasurer and Trustee, served 10.5 years on the Oakland County School Board Association Board of Directors including two years as OCSBA President, earned the MASB Board Member Presidents Award (Level 7) requiring a minimum of 29 advanced level 200 and 300 courses and 1,383 education credits, with actual CBA credits of 207 and education credits of 1,995, received the NSBA Distinguished Service Award, attended 17 Federal Relations Network Conferences in Washington, DC, and has worked at Kaplan Professional Education since 1983 as Senior Instructor/Training Manager conducting seminars for 19 FINRA securities licenses; he served as one of eight Optimist International Vice Presidents in 2009-2010, conducted over 50 training sessions at the Optimist International Convention, received the Level X Personal Growth and Achievement Award and is a member of the Michigan District Optimist Hall of Fame. Mr. Charles Hemple, Hazel Park Board of Education Secretary (chuck.hemple@hazelpark.k12.mi.us), moved to Hazel Park in 1980, graduated from Hazel Park High School in 1985, attended Macomb Community College and the Local 80 Training Center, has spent fourteen years in Sheet Metal Workers Union Local 80, has been married to Sue for 19 years and has three children, Chuckie 15, Zack 10 and Raelyn 5, and serves as a Precinct Delegate for the Democratic Party of Hazel Park. Mr. George R. Ehlert, President of the Oakland Schools Board of Education (Gehlert@comcast.net), is completing his 6th year, having been appointed in September 2003 after board resignations resulting from the Redmond scandal, serving through June 2008 and being reappointed in December 2010; he served over 17 years on the South Lyon Board of Education, retired from Ehlert/Bryan, Inc., a consulting engineering firm he founded over 30 years ago, has been married to Georganne for 33 years and has 3 grown children, and states the board directs over 94% of its resources toward local districts. Bob Klein of 2974 Shawnee Lane, Waterford, Michigan 48329, an 18-year resident married 21 years with three children, holds a 1993 Master's Degree in Administration from Central Michigan University and a 1984 BS from the University of Michigan plus University of Michigan certificates in Lean Product and Process and Lean Manufacturing; employed at Chrysler LLC, he managed the technical education of approximately 6000 engineers, designers and quality staff for 11 years, served 3 years on the Oakland Schools Manufacturing Advisory Committee, gained Chrysler sponsorship for the SAE Super Mileage Event at the Eaton Proving Grounds in Marshall, MI, taught high school math and science on St Croix in the US Virgin Islands, and is a US Navy veteran seeking votes at the June 4, 2012 Oakland Schools Election.
